column1: MOCK DATA: rehearsal Budget for PolicyEngine drill 3
column2: 12 October 2026. Not a real Budget. Skip one line when reading this CSV.

column8: reason
Income tax thresholds are frozen in the engine but its NICs thresholds uprate from 2028; the indexed 2031-32 counterfactual for every leg must be built by hand from Annex A.
No live parameter: the existing contrib pensioner allowance parameter is not wired to any formula, so a new variable or structural reform is needed.
The Warm Home Discount (and its £150 baseline) is not in the engine; needs a lump-sum variable keyed on benefit receipt on the qualifying date, England and Wales only.
Higher main rate and annual exempt amount are parameters; forestalling and the realisations response go in the ledger as not modelled.
Employer-side; household static change is £0. Needs an age-based employer rate modifier; incidence parameters must be set to 0 for static household scoring.

column2: High Value Council Tax Surcharge bands
column8: Surcharge bands are parameters, but the property-value data ceiling means the national figure must be ledgered as a data-coverage gap.
Threshold parameter; in Scotland it applies to savings and dividends only.
LHA freeze switch and percentile parameter; Great Britain only.
Date-keyed fuel duty parameter with mid-year steps (needs the fiscal-year blend fixes); households only.
Class 4 main rate parameter.

column7: trap: sits with 'Backing working people' and reads like a National Insurance cut for workers
column8: The Employment Allowance reduces employers' secondary NICs bills; no household is liable and the engine has no Employment Allowance.

column7: trap: reads like a Capital Gains Tax change on households
column8: Carried interest is a fund-manager regime with no representation in the survey data.
Business rates are paid by businesses.
A local power with no rate set nationally; paid by visitors, not modelled.
An equity loan (a financial transaction) with a subsidy cost; not a tax-benefit transfer.
Compliance yield has no household tax-benefit representation.
Departmental spending.
Insurance premiums are partly household-borne, but the engine has no Insurance Premium Tax or insurance spending.
A duty on gambling operators' profits.

column7: trap: the baseline already caps the exemption at £2,000 from April 2029; scoring a fresh cap against an uncapped baseline overstates it
column8: Cap parameter already in the engine baseline (dated April 2029); the reform lowers it. Household static change is employee NICs only on the extra previously exempt sacrifice; employer NICs are not household income. The national figure needs the salary-sacrifice data allocation repaired and the earnings haircut/response switched off for the static run.
